title: 码表数据上传第三方平台（Strava / TrainingPeaks / TrainerRoad）后字段缺失或同步中断
problem_statement: 用户在码表上记录了完整的骑行数据（含心率、踏频等），但通过自动同步上传到 Strava、TrainingPeaks、TrainerRoad 等第三方平台后，出现两类问题：(1) 部分字段（如心率）为空，只有基础的距离和时间；(2) 自动同步功能完全失效，需改为手动上传。
root_cause_hypotheses: 码表固件与第三方平台（Strava/TrainingPeaks/TrainerRoad）之间的数据字段映射存在缺失或兼容性问题，导致心率、踏频等次要字段在同步链路中被丢弃。
码表与第三方平台之间的自动同步通道（OAuth token、API 连接）在数月前发生过中断或令牌过期/失效，且缺少自动续期或失效提示机制，从而完全停止工作。
App 端自动上传功能的配置项可能被默认更改或与新版固件不兼容，用户既无明确入口恢复自动同步，也未收到错误通知。
counter_evidence: ["证据 F0006 提到自动同步在'a few months ago'前正常工作，提示问题可能由近期外部变更（Strava/TrainingPeaks 接口或策略）引起，而非码表本身长期缺陷；目前尚无证据可证实是哪一方变更触发。", "证据 F0040 用户为询问'能否连接'的语气，说明 Magene 与 TrainerRoad 的官方连接支持状态本就不明确，不能直接归因为 Bug；需先确认是否属于功能缺失。", '心率字段为空也可能源自用户账号隐私设置或活动类型（如室内训练）而非同步故障，目前证据未排除这一可能。', '三条证据来自不同用户、不同使用场景，可能分别对应不同根因，不能简单假设它们由同一故障引起。']

recommended_actions.action: 在码表端导出原始活动文件（FIT/TCX），与上传到 Strava 后解析得到的数据进行字段级 diff，定位是字段映射丢失还是文件解析问题。

title: 心率在低活动段持续高估拍数
problem_statement: 在用户活动量较低的时段，心率监测设备连续多拍过度计数，导致读数在相当长的一段时期内偏离实际心率（用户原文：'not always accurate. hr sometimes way overcounts beats for stretches of time when minimal effort is …'）。簇内仅 1 条 S3 证据，优先级分数 13，问题影响范围有限但用户体验受损明显。
root_cause_hypotheses: 信号采集侧：在低活动、低心率区间，光电（PPG）传感器的信号幅度较弱，运动伪影阈值或增益设置使算法将噪声误识别为脉搏波峰，引发过度计数。
算法侧：低活动时段心率波形形态改变（峰间距拉长、波形平坦），现有波峰检测/频率估计逻辑未充分适配该区段，缺少针对低活动模式的滤波或拒绝阈值。
运动状态判定侧：活动量识别未将“极低活动”与“正常活动”区分开，触发统一的计拍分支，导致误检。
counter_evidence: ['簇内仅含 1 条 S3 证据，样本量不足以确认问题在一般用户群体中的普遍性，可能是个别佩戴或环境因素导致的偶发体验。', "证据原文被截断（'when minimal effort is …'），未明确触发场景的持续时长、活动类型与发生频率，难以判断是稳定缺陷还是边界用例。", '未提供该时段的心率真值对照，无法排除用户主观感受与设备读数偏差的范围；若真实心率本身存在波动，读数差异可能被放大描述。', '未涉及不同固件/硬件版本的差异，尚不明确是当前版本回归还是历史遗留问题。']

recommended_actions.action: 复现并量化低活动段过度计数的复现条件（佩戴松紧、活动类型、信号质量指标），采集对应原始 PPG/加速度波形作为基线。

title: Route Planner Usability Issues Causing App Instability and User Friction
problem_statement: Users consistently value the app's core value propositions — accurate bike-lane routing, comprehensive route planning, and offline/turn-by-turn navigation — but report meaningful friction in exercising those features. Across 15 pieces of evidence, recurring complaints describe the route planner as hard to use, non-functional, or non-intuitive, navigation on saved routes as erratic, and at least one reported app crash during route execution on a paid offline workflow. The contradiction between high feature love and high reported difficulty signals a usability and stability gap on the primary user journey.
root_cause_hypotheses: Route planner UX has a discoverability/affordance gap: users struggle to complete basic route creation on first attempts (evidence: F0166 — 'tried about 10x to make it work'), suggesting the workflow is not self-evident and lacks adequate onboarding or empty-state guidance.

Saved-route navigation behavior diverges from user mental model: users describe saved-route navigation as 'wonky' and report 'weird quirks' (F0157, F0184), suggesting state transitions between planning, saving, and following a route have unclear or inconsistent UX cues.

Route planner has functional defects that block task completion: 'Route planner just doesn't work!' (F0163) and 'half stuck that crashes the app' (F0170) indicate at least some users hit hard failures, not only learning-curve issues — possibly tied to edge cases in saved/imported routes, offline mode, or large route graphs.
counter_evidence: ["Multiple users explicitly praise the route planner and the app's core navigation value (F0144, F0148, F0155, F0168, F0182), indicating the feature works well for a non-trivial segment and the issues above may be concentrated in specific flows or user segments rather than the planner as a whole.", "Some reported friction is self-attributed to user learning curve rather than product defect (F0157: 'More to learn I guess'), suggesting at least part of the difficulty is onboarding-related and not all 'wonky' behavior is a functional bug.", "The cluster contains 15 pieces of evidence but only a small subset explicitly report crashes or total failure (F0163, F0170); the dominant theme is 'hard to use' rather than 'broken,' which limits certainty about engineering root causes vs. UX root causes."]
